title: My Daily Routine
description: Talk about what you do every day from morning to night using the present simple.
focus: By the end of today, you can describe your complete daily routine — morning, afternoon, evening and night — in clear present simple sentences.

grammar.title: Present Simple
grammar.explanation: We use the present simple for habits and routines — things we do again and again. With I, you, we and they, the verb stays the same. With he, she and it, we add -s to the verb. We use do and does for questions and negatives.

structures.pattern: I / You / We / They do not (don't) + verb
structures.label: Negative

structures.pattern: He / She / It does not (doesn't) + verb
structures.label: Negative

structures.pattern: Do + I / you / we / they + verb ...?
structures.label: Question

examples.sentence: I wake up at seven every day.
She usually eats cereal for breakfast.
He works in a big office and starts at nine.
We do not (don't) watch television at night.
My sister never goes to bed late.
Do you walk to work every day?
They arrive at eight o'clock and start immediately.

commonUsage: Habits and routines: I eat breakfast at eight.
How often: always, usually, sometimes, never — I always sleep eight hours.
Schedules and fixed times: The train leaves at half past six.

commonMistakes.note: With I, you, we and they, the verb has no -s.
With he, she and it, use doesn't, not don't.

commonMistakes.wrong: Does she works in a bank?
commonMistakes.right: Does she work in a bank?
commonMistakes.note: After does, use the base verb without -s.

commonMistakes.wrong: I am wake up early every day.
commonMistakes.right: I wake up early every day.
commonMistakes.note: Routines use the present simple, not am/is/are + verb.

vocabulary.definition: to stop sleeping and open your eyes
vocabulary.example: I wake up at seven every morning.

vocabulary.definition: to leave your bed after sleeping
vocabulary.example: After I wake up, I get up and open the window.

vocabulary.definition: a clock or phone that makes a sound to wake you
vocabulary.example: My alarm rings at six thirty.

vocabulary.definition: to clean your teeth with a toothbrush
vocabulary.example: I brush my teeth after breakfast.

vocabulary.definition: water that falls on you to wash your body, or the act of washing this way
vocabulary.example: I take a shower before I get dressed.

vocabulary.definition: to put on your clothes
vocabulary.example: I get dressed quickly in the morning.

vocabulary.definition: the first meal of the day, in the morning
vocabulary.example: I eat breakfast with my family at eight.

vocabulary.definition: a hot dark drink that helps you feel awake
vocabulary.example: I drink one cup of coffee every morning.

vocabulary.definition: a breakfast food eaten with cold milk
vocabulary.example: She usually eats cereal with milk for breakfast.

vocabulary.definition: to put things into a bag or suitcase
vocabulary.example: I pack my bag and leave the house at seven.

vocabulary.definition: to go away from a place
vocabulary.example: I leave the house at half past seven.

vocabulary.definition: to move on your feet
vocabulary.example: I walk to work every day.

vocabulary.definition: to do your job, or the place where you do it
vocabulary.example: I work in a small office near my home.

vocabulary.definition: to get to a place
vocabulary.example: I arrive at work at eight o'clock.

vocabulary.definition: to begin something
vocabulary.example: I start work at half past eight.

vocabulary.definition: having a lot of things to do
vocabulary.example: I am busy all morning, so I eat lunch late.

vocabulary.definition: to look at something to see if it is okay
vocabulary.example: First, I check my emails and messages.

vocabulary.definition: a message you send using the internet
vocabulary.example: I check my email before I start work.

vocabulary.definition: the meal you eat in the middle of the day
vocabulary.example: I eat lunch at one o'clock with my friends.

vocabulary.definition: the time between midday and the evening
vocabulary.example: I am very busy in the afternoon.

vocabulary.definition: to complete something; to come to the end
vocabulary.example: I finish work at five and walk home.

vocabulary.definition: feeling that you need rest or sleep
vocabulary.example: After work, I am too tired to cook.

vocabulary.definition: feeling that you want to eat
vocabulary.example: I am always hungry at lunchtime.

vocabulary.definition: the time between the end of the afternoon and bedtime
vocabulary.example: In the evening, I cook dinner and relax.

vocabulary.definition: the main meal of the day, eaten in the evening
vocabulary.example: We eat dinner together at eight.

vocabulary.definition: to make food hot and ready to eat
vocabulary.example: I usually cook rice and vegetables for dinner.

vocabulary.definition: to clean something with water
vocabulary.example: I wash the dishes after dinner.

vocabulary.definition: plates, bowls, cups and other things used for food
vocabulary.example: There are many dishes in the sink after dinner.

vocabulary.definition: clothes that need washing, or the act of washing them
vocabulary.example: I do the laundry twice a week.

vocabulary.definition: to look at something for a time, like a program or game
vocabulary.example: We watch television after dinner.

vocabulary.definition: a device with a screen that shows programs; also the programs themselves
vocabulary.example: My favorite program is on television tonight.

vocabulary.definition: to rest and stop feeling worried
vocabulary.example: In the evening, I relax with a book.

vocabulary.definition: to go to shops to buy things
vocabulary.example: On Fridays, we go shopping for food.

vocabulary.definition: the dark time between evening and morning
vocabulary.example: I am always tired on Tuesday nights.

vocabulary.definition: the usual time when you go to bed
vocabulary.example: My bedtime is eleven o'clock.

vocabulary.definition: to get into bed to sleep
vocabulary.example: I go to bed at eleven and sleep eight hours.

vocabulary.definition: to rest with your eyes closed and your mind not awake
vocabulary.example: I usually sleep eight hours every night.

vocabulary.definition: most of the time, but not always
vocabulary.example: I usually eat cereal for breakfast.

vocabulary.definition: every time; all the time
vocabulary.example: I always sleep eight hours.

vocabulary.definition: on some days or occasions, but not often and not never
vocabulary.example: Sometimes I eat lunch with my friends.

vocabulary.definition: at no time; not even once
vocabulary.example: I never go to bed before midnight.

vocabulary.definition: near the beginning of the day or before the usual time
vocabulary.example: On Tuesdays, I wake up very early.

vocabulary.definition: after the usual time or expected time
vocabulary.example: I am never late for work.

vocabulary.definition: each day, without missing one
vocabulary.example: I walk to work every day.

vocabulary.definition: used after a number to say the exact hour
vocabulary.example: I arrive at work at eight o'clock.

vocabulary.example: I start work at half past eight.

vocabulary.definition: happening every day

conversations.title: Morning Routine
conversations.setting: Two friends, Maya and Sam, talk on the phone in the morning.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Hi Sam! It's eight o'clock. Are you awake?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Almost. My alarm rings at seven, but I usually wake up at seven fifteen.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: That's late! I always wake up at six. Then I get up, I brush my teeth, and I take a shower.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I know, I know. I'm never early. After my shower, I get dressed and make breakfast.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: What do you eat in the morning?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Usually cereal with milk and a big cup of coffee.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Nice. I only drink coffee. Then I pack my bag and leave the house at seven.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Do you walk to work every day?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Yes, I walk every day. It's twenty minutes, and I arrive at eight.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: You start work at eight? Wow. OK, I need to hurry. Talk later!

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: OK! Don't be late again.

conversations.title: A Busy Day at Work
conversations.setting: Two colleagues, Lina and Omar, eat lunch together at work.

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: I'm so tired. I checked forty emails before ten o'clock.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Me too. My day starts at half past eight, and this morning I arrived late.

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: What time do you usually arrive at work?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: At half past eight. But I never finish before six.

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: That's a long day. Are you busy this afternoon?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Very busy. I have a lot of work, and I check my email every hour.

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: Let's eat lunch quickly then. I'm really hungry.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Good idea. I always eat lunch at one o'clock.

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: And after lunch? More work?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Work, work, work until six. Then I walk home, cook dinner and relax.

lines.speaker: Lina
lines.text: You cook every night? I'm too tired to cook in the evening.

conversations.title: Evening Plans
conversations.setting: Two roommates, Nora and Adam, talk in the kitchen in the evening.

lines.speaker: Nora
lines.text: What do you usually do in the evening?

lines.speaker: Adam
lines.text: Nothing special. I watch television and relax on the sofa.

lines.speaker: Nora
lines.text: I cook dinner at seven. Do you want to eat with me?

lines.speaker: Adam
lines.text: Sure. I can wash the dishes after dinner.

lines.speaker: Nora
lines.text: Great. And do we need food? I go shopping on Fridays, but the fridge is empty.

lines.speaker: Adam
lines.text: It's full. I did the laundry and cleaned today too.

lines.speaker: Nora
lines.text: Nice. What time is your bedtime? You look tired.

lines.speaker: Adam
lines.text: I never go to bed before midnight. But I have a good habit: I sleep eight hours.

lines.speaker: Nora
lines.text: I have a different habit. I always sleep late, but I am free in the morning!

lines.speaker: Adam
lines.text: Every day is different in this house. OK, dinner first, television after.

lines.speaker: Nora
lines.text: Deal. Dinner at half past seven, and a movie at nine.

paragraphs.title: My Typical Day
paragraphs.text: I wake up at six thirty every day. First, I brush my teeth and take a quick shower. Then I get dressed and make breakfast. I usually eat cereal with milk and drink one cup of coffee. At seven thirty, I pack my bag and leave the house. I walk to work and arrive at eight. I start work at half past eight and check my emails. I am busy all morning. I eat lunch at one o'clock, sometimes with my friends. I finish work at five and walk home. In the evening, I cook dinner and relax. My bedtime is eleven o'clock, so I always sleep eight hours.

paragraphs.title: A Busy Tuesday
paragraphs.text: On Tuesdays, my daily routine is different. My alarm rings at five thirty, so I wake up very early. I get up, drink coffee, and leave home at six fifteen. I arrive at work before seven and start immediately. The office is busy all day, and I check a hundred emails. I eat lunch at my desk and finish at four. After work, I go shopping because there is no food at home. In the evening, I cook a big dinner, wash the dishes, and watch television for one hour. I am always tired on Tuesday nights, so I go to bed early and sleep well.

paragraphs.title: Evenings at Home
paragraphs.text: In the evening, our home is calm. My sister and I cook dinner together. She usually cooks rice and chicken, and I wash the dishes after dinner. Then we relax. She watches her favorite program on television, and I read or listen to music. Twice a week, I do the laundry in the evening, and on Fridays we go shopping for food. We are free after nine o'clock, and we sometimes talk about our day. At half past ten, my sister goes to bed, but I often sleep late. I am never tired at bedtime — I am a night person.
